q: What's the difference between the FOMC and the Board of Governors?
label: Answered by Gemini Flash
text: The Board of Governors is a permanent, seven-member body in Washington that oversees the entire Federal Reserve System. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is the specific group of twelve members—including all seven governors—that meets eight times a year to decide interest rates and monetary policy.

label: Answered by Gemini Flash
text: The Federal Reserve was created by Congress in 1913 to serve as the central bank of the United States. Its main purpose is to manage the nation's monetary policy under a dual mandate to pursue maximum employment and stable prices.

q: What's the fed funds rate right now?
label: Answered by Gemini Flash
text: The Federal Reserve set the federal funds rate target range at "4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent" at its November 2024 meeting. The FOMC lowered the rate by 1/4 percentage point to support maximum employment and return inflation to its 2 percent goal.

q: Who votes on the FOMC this year?
label: Answered by Gemini Flash
text: The FOMC has 12 voting members: the seven members of the Board of Governors, the president of the New York Fed, and four regional bank presidents who serve on a rotating basis.
